item.title: Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch — Mon Nov 2, 10:00 AM — Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch
item.description:
Located in the small west Marin village of Nicasio, the farm is just west of the Nicasio Village Square right on Nicasio Valley Road. Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch is open seven days a week through Halloween from 10 am to 6 pm weekends and 10 am to 4 pm during the week, and it's always worth a visit. It's been a Marin County tradition for over 20 years! Nicasio Valley Pumpkin Patch offers a wide variety of pumpkins spread out in an expansive meadow on the farm. Pumpkin varieties ranged from your standard Halloween jack-o-lantern types to white ones, green Italian and Australian varieties, and flat European "Cinderella" style squash. The farmstand also offers of gourds, squash, and decorative cornstalks, apples, as well as drinks and snacks. Pumpkins range in price from $8 to $44. Admission is Free, Pumpkins are Priced Individually
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: The Arts Guild of Sonoma Presents: Thanks to Art — Wed Nov 4, 5:00 PM — Arts Guild of Sonoma
item.description:
“Thanks to Art” at the Arts Guild of Sonoma | November 4–30
Celebrate the creativity of local artists at the Arts Guild of Sonoma’s November exhibition, “Thanks to Art.” Featured Member Artist Susan Heeringa-Pieper presents imaginative mixed-media works, while Guest Artist Rebecca Plachte-Zuieback showcases intricate textile collages created from reclaimed fabrics. Discover original paintings, sculpture, ceramics, jewelry, photography, and more. Voted People's Choice Best Gallery. The Arts Guild of Sonoma is a cooperative gallery showcasing the work of its member artists alongside selected guest artists and special features. With a continually changing collection and a wide range of media and price points, the Guild offers an ongoing opportunity to discover original art in Sonoma.
Opening Reception: Saturday, November 4, 5–7:30 PM. Free and open to the public.
Location: 140 East Napa Street, Sonoma. Open Wednesday–Monday, 11 AM–5 PM. Free admission.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Nov 5, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: Why Are We Sprinting Off The AI Cliff? — Thu Nov 5, 4:00 PM — Springstowne Library
item.description:
This is a a free and open event - we'll watch a video and learn together, then discuss our opinions. You'll come away with a better understanding of AI and develop your own ideas about this transformational technology. AI companies are racing to build systems that can improve themselves, even though they admit that they have zero confidence in being able to control them. Journalist Ezra Klein explains the recent HuggingFace incident, and how this might be a warning shot that the public should pay attention to. Join a friendly, beginner conversation on the current state of AI and where we might be headed. You'll come away with enough information to build your own opinion about AI. No registration required, but if you would like an e-mail reminder you can sign up to receive one.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Frank Lloyd Wright Civic Center Tours — Fri Nov 6, 10:30 AM — Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Adult $10, Senior/Full Time Student $5 \(Plus a $2 p er ticket service Charge Online\)
Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Cuentos con Ritmo (Stories with Rhythm) — Thu Nov 12, 10:30 AM — Children’s Museum of Sonoma County
item.description:
Cuentos con Ritmo (Stories with Rhythm)
Cuentos con Ritmo | Cuentos * Música * Movimiento
Presentado por Colors of Spanish
Cuentos con Ritmo es una oportunidad única semanal para niños de 1 a 5 años y sus familias, el cual aporta alegría, comprensión y aprecio por la lengua española a toda la comunidad. Durante Cuentos con Ritmo, los pequeños visitantes y sus familias participan de forma lúdica en historias interactivas con música y movimiento fortaleciendo nuestra diversa comunidad y entusiasmo por la lengua meta.
Cuentos con Ritmo es presentado por Guadalupe Tausch en colaboración con la organización que fundó, Colors of Spanish. Originaria del estado de Guanajuato en México, tiene una maestría en español con énfasis en la adquisición de una segunda lengua para la primera infancia y continúa sus estudios enfocada en la primera infancia especializándose en la adquisición de idiomas a través de la música/movimiento. Colors of Spanish ofrece talleres para profesores,
